userStories.title: Add pycronometer and analysis dependencies
userStories.description: Add pycronometer library from GitHub, cryptography for Fernet encryption, numpy and scipy for statistical analysis to backend/pyproject.toml dependencies.

userStories.title: Create CronometerCredential model
userStories.description: Create SQLAlchemy model for storing encrypted Cronometer credentials. Fields: id (UUID), user_id (FK to users), encrypted_email (Text), encrypted_password (Text), last_sync_at (datetime nullable), created_at, updated_at. Add relationship to User model.
acceptanceCriteria: Foreign key to users table with CASCADE delete
user_id is unique (one credential per user)

userStories.title: Create FoodLog model
userStories.description: Create SQLAlchemy model for storing food servings from Cronometer. Fields: id, user_id, logged_at, food_name, serving_size, food_group (nullable), calories, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g, sugar_g, sodium_mg, raw_data (JSONB), cronometer_hash (unique for dedup), created_at.
acceptanceCriteria: raw_data field uses JSONB type from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql
cronometer_hash is unique and indexed for deduplication
logged_at is indexed for date range queries

userStories.title: Create BiometricLog model
userStories.description: Create SQLAlchemy model for storing biometric measurements. Fields: id, user_id, logged_at, metric_type (string), value (float), unit (string), raw_data (JSONB), cronometer_hash (unique), created_at.
acceptanceCriteria: metric_type stores the type like 'weight', 'body_fat', etc.

userStories.title: Create HealthNote model
userStories.description: Create SQLAlchemy model for storing notes including bowel movements. Fields: id, user_id, logged_at, content (Text), is_bowel_movement (bool), bristol_scale (int 1-7 nullable), quantity_score (int 1-10 nullable), raw_data (JSONB), cronometer_hash (unique), created_at.
acceptanceCriteria: bristol_scale and quantity_score are nullable for non-BM notes

userStories.title: Create Alembic migration for Cronometer tables
userStories.description: Generate and verify Alembic migration for the 4 new tables: cronometer_credentials, food_logs, biometric_logs, health_notes. Ensure proper indexes and constraints.
acceptanceCriteria: Alembic migration file created in backend/alembic/versions/
Migration creates food_logs table with JSONB column
All foreign keys and indexes are properly defined
Migration can be applied with alembic upgrade head

userStories.title: Create encryption utility module
userStories.description: Create utility module for encrypting/decrypting Cronometer credentials using Fernet symmetric encryption. Include functions: encrypt_string, decrypt_string. Read key from CRONOMETER_ENCRYPTION_KEY env var.

userStories.title: Create Cronometer sync service - core structure
userStories.description: Create the CronometerSyncService class with init, sync_user method skeleton, and helper methods for getting credentials and generating hashes. Do not implement the upsert methods yet.
acceptanceCriteria: sync_user(user_id: UUID, days_back: int = 7) -> SyncResult method skeleton
_get_credentials(user_id) method that queries DB and decrypts
SyncResult dataclass defined with food_logs_synced, biometric_logs_synced, health_notes_synced counts

userStories.title: Implement sync service - food logs upsert
userStories.description: Implement _upsert_food_logs method in CronometerSyncService. Transform pycronometer Serving objects to FoodLog models, use cronometer_hash for deduplication (skip existing).
acceptanceCriteria: Generates hash from serving raw_data for deduplication
Skips servings that already exist (by hash)
Maps all fields from Serving to FoodLog including raw_data
Returns list of newly created FoodLog objects

userStories.title: Implement sync service - biometric logs upsert
userStories.description: Implement _upsert_biometric_logs method in CronometerSyncService. Transform pycronometer BiometricEntry objects to BiometricLog models with deduplication.
acceptanceCriteria: Generates hash from entry raw_data for deduplication
Skips entries that already exist (by hash)
Maps metric, value, unit fields correctly
Returns list of newly created BiometricLog objects

userStories.title: Implement sync service - health notes with BM parsing
userStories.description: Implement _upsert_health_notes method and _parse_bowel_movement helper. Parse note content for 'Bowel Movement' keyword, extract Bristol scale and quantity score using regex.
acceptanceCriteria: Extracts Bristol scale with regex like 'bristol\s*(\d)'
Sets is_bowel_movement, bristol_scale, quantity_score on HealthNote

userStories.title: Complete sync_user method with pycronometer integration
userStories.description: Complete the sync_user method to use pycronometer client: login with decrypted credentials, fetch servings/biometrics/notes, call upsert methods, update last_sync_at timestamp.
acceptanceCriteria: Calls get_servings, get_biometrics, get_notes with date range

userStories.title: Create Pydantic schemas for Cronometer API
userStories.description: Create Pydantic schemas for API requests and responses: SaveCredentialsRequest, SyncRequest, SyncResponse, FoodLogResponse, HealthNoteResponse, CredentialStatusResponse.
acceptanceCriteria: SyncResponse with food_logs_synced, biometric_logs_synced, health_notes_synced, synced_at

userStories.title: Create Cronometer credentials API endpoints

acceptanceCriteria: POST /credentials saves encrypted email/password for current user
GET /credentials/status returns whether credentials exist and last sync time
DELETE /credentials removes credentials for current user

userStories.title: Create Cronometer sync API endpoint
userStories.description: Create POST /api/cronometer/sync endpoint that triggers a manual sync for the current user using CronometerSyncService.
acceptanceCriteria: Returns SyncResponse with counts and timestamp
Returns 404 if user has no credentials saved
Returns appropriate error if Cronometer login fails

userStories.title: Create food logs and health notes read endpoints

userStories.title: Create InsightsService - core structure and types
